title: Tetra-covalency, Catenation and Classification
notes: **Tetra-covalency:** carbon shares four electrons to complete its octet, giving it four bonds. This allows chain, branched, and ring structures.
**Catenation:** carbon-carbon bonds are strong (348 kJ/mol for C-C), allowing long chains. C-C bond strength decreases down the group: Si-Si (222), Ge-Ge (167), Sn-Sn (122) kJ/mol.
**Classification by carbon skeleton:** acyclic/open chain (straight or branched) and cyclic/closed chain (homocyclic: C only; heterocyclic: C + O/N/S).
**Classification by functional groups:** alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alcohols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amides, amines, etc.
**Homologous series:** groups of compounds with same functional group and similar chemical properties, differing by $CH_2$ unit in molecular formula.
